required_facts.fact: In 2177, an Alliance Marine unit is sent to investigate the settlement at Akuze, a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space, after all contact is lost with the pioneer team. The unit arrives to find the settlement intact but completely abandoned—no survivors are found. When the unit establishes camp for the night, they are attacked by subterranean thresher maws, creatures the Alliance has never encountered before. The unit is nearly completely slaughtered in the attack, with fifty marines killed and only one known survivor reaching the landing zone alive. If Commander Shepard is that sole survivor, Shepard is permanently marked by the trauma. Years later, Corporal Toombs is discovered to have also survived the attack. Toombs reveals a shocking truth: the massacre was not an accident. According to Toombs' testimony, the renegade black ops group Cerberus deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines as part of an experiment to study the creatures and observe how the unit responded to an unknown threat. Toombs was captured by Cerberus after the attack and subjected to horrific ordeals including being injected with thresher maw acid as part of their research. The revelation that Cerberus orchestrated the massacre haunts Shepard throughout the trilogy, becoming a symbol of Cerberus's willingness to sacrifice human lives for their research agenda.

During Cerberus's 2186 coup attempt on the Citadel (Priority: The Citadel II), Councilor Udina moved the Citadel Council toward a waiting escape shuttle while the Cerberus assassin Kai Leng hunted them. The salarian councilor - Valern, or Esheel if Valern had died on Sur'Kesh - hid under tactical cloak in the executor's cafe/office area after the executor was killed. When Commander Shepard's squad located him, he began to reveal that Udina was orchestrating the coup, and Kai Leng arrived to silence him. What happened next depended on who was still alive to intervene (per `citadel_coup` and `salarian_councilor`). If Thane Krios had survived the 2185 Suicide Mission and Shepard had visited him at Huerta Memorial Hospital before this mission, Thane dropped in and fought Kai Leng hand to hand, buying time and saving the councilor but taking Leng's blade through the torso. If Thane was absent but Major Kirrahe had survived Virmire in 2183 (per `kirrahe_virmire`), a cloaked Kirrahe took the shot meant for the councilor, then limped a short distance before collapsing and dying on the spot; as he was never Normandy crew, his name does not appear on the memorial wall. If neither was present - or no Mass Effect 2 save was imported - Kai Leng killed the salarian councilor outright. In every case Leng then fled, disabled Shepard's pursuit skycar with his sword, and ultimately escaped the failed coup. A mortally wounded Thane was taken to Huerta Memorial. Shepard could be present for his final moments, where his estranged son Kolyat joined them regardless of the outcome of Thane: Sins of the Father. In the last stage of Kepral's Syndrome, Thane died in surgery as Kolyat and Shepard recited the drell prayer to Kalahira; Thane revealed the prayer had been his wish for Shepard, not himself. His name was added to the Normandy's memorial wall. If Thane had survived Mass Effect 2 but was never visited at the hospital, he did not appear at the coup at all, yet his name still turned up on the memorial wall afterward. Shepard later avenged him by killing Kai Leng at Cerberus Headquarters.
Per `citadel_coup`/`salarian_councilor`: if Thane was alive and visited at Huerta, he intercepts Kai Leng, saves the salarian councilor, and is fatally stabbed

To seal the turian-krogan alliance, the Urdnot leader (Wrex or Wreav) demands the genophage be cured. Once Mordin Solus or Padok Wiks has stabilised Eve and prepared the cure, Shepard leads a joint turian-krogan strike on Tuchanka to disperse it through the Shroud, the atmospheric tower above the krogan homeworld. Before the operation, Dalatrass Linron privately offers Shepard a deal: the salarians will back the war effort if Shepard lets Mordin secretly sabotage the cure, keeping the krogan weakened. Shepard can accept, refuse, or tell the krogan leader. The krogan convoy drives for the Shroud but is halted when Kalros, the largest known thresher maw, is roused in the catacombs beneath an abandoned krogan city and destroys a bridge. A Reaper Destroyer guards the Shroud. Eve proposes activating the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros against the Reaper while the cure is completed. Shepard activates the hammers; Kalros drags the Destroyer down. The Shroud is left damaged and unstable, and the cure must be released manually from the top of the collapsing tower. The outcome is choice-conditional. If Shepard preserved Maelon's data in Mass Effect 2 (per `mordin_loyalty`) and did not accept the sabotage, Eve survives the procedure and the krogan gain a healthy future. If Maelon's data was destroyed, Eve dies of complications regardless. If Mordin is alive and the cure is genuine, he insists on going up the tower himself and is killed when it detonates, singing as he dies; if the cure is sabotaged and Mordin realises, Shepard can shoot him, or he goes up to fix it and dies anyway. If Padok Wiks replaced Mordin, Wiks dies in the tower. A sabotaged cure can also be carried out with the krogan none the wiser, especially under Wreav (per `genophage`: cured, or secretly sabotaged). Whatever happens, the Reaper guarding the Shroud is destroyed and the krogan commit forces to the war; a genuine cure earns their full strength, while sabotage risks later exposure.
The Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud is dragged down and killed by the thresher maw Kalros
Per `genophage`: the genophage is genuinely cured, or secretly sabotaged by Mordin at the Dalatrass's request
Per `mordin_loyalty`: Eve survives the cure if Maelon's data was preserved, otherwise she dies of complications

The salarian scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks if Mordin is dead) is usually killed in the collapsing Shroud tower completing the cure; Mordin can instead be shot by Shepard if he insists on fixing a sabotage
The Shroud tower is destroyed
The krogan join the war against the Reapers; a true cure yields full krogan support, sabotage risks a later rebellion
Per `krogan_leader`: under Wrex the krogan become steadfast allies; under Wreav they are more belligerent
If cured and Wrex lives, Eve later carries Wrex's children and helps rebuild krogan society

In 2186 the quarian Migrant Fleet launched an all-out war to retake Rannoch, catching the geth mid-construction of their megastructure. When the flotilla bombarded and destroyed the structure, killing many programs and dimming the consensus, the surviving geth accepted Reaper code and Reaper upgrades to survive - which turned the war in their favour and pushed the quarians to the brink. Both fleets appealed to Commander Shepard. Shepard first infiltrated a geth dreadnought over Rannoch and freed Legion (or, if Legion was lost, a Geth VI) that had been wired into the drive core as the Reapers' signal booster, shutting the dreadnought down. Shepard then made planetfall and, painting the target for orbital fire, destroyed the Reaper on the surface that was broadcasting the control signal, freeing the geth fleet from Reaper command; dialogue lets Shepard frame this as vengeance for the pre-Prothean species harvested to build that Reaper. With the geth free but the quarians still attacking, Legion sought to upload the Reaper-derived code to grant every geth true individual consciousness, while Tali'Zorah feared it would doom her people. Shepard moderated the standoff (per `geth_quarian` and `rannoch`). Allowing the upload without brokering peace gives the geth full sentience and their fleet to the war but sees the quarian fleet destroyed, with Admiral Koris and Tali possibly lost. Refusing the upload wipes out the geth and leaves the quarians to reclaim Rannoch. A successful reputation check - requiring Legion alive, both Tali and Legion loyal, the heretics rewritten and the Tali/Legion history reconciled - brokers a ceasefire: the geth help the quarians resettle Rannoch, some even uploading into quarian suits to rebuild their immune systems, and both fleets join the war. In every branch the unit (Legion or the Geth VI) sacrifices itself to complete or enable the upload.
The geth dreadnought is disabled and the Reaper directing the geth on Rannoch is destroyed, freeing the geth fleet from Reaper control
Per `geth_quarian`/`rannoch`: the geth gain true consciousness and survive, or the geth are wiped out, or geth and quarians make peace and co-exist on Rannoch
Allowing the upload without peace destroys the quarian fleet; Admiral Koris and Tali may die
Refusing the upload exterminates the geth and hands Rannoch back to the quarians
Brokered peace requires Legion alive plus loyal, reconciled Tali and Legion, and adds both the Geth Fleet and Quarian Fleet as war assets
Legion or the Geth VI sacrifices itself in every outcome
The pre-Prothean species harvested to create the Rannoch Reaper is symbolically avenged

evidence.text: If Commander Shepard is a survivor of Akuze, there is a news announcement about a Shepard Memorial being erected on Akuze, and that once the site is cleared of thresher maws, a commemoration ceremony hosted by Admiral Steven Hackett will be held in 2186\. If Shepard rescued Toombs in 2183, the Commander will receive a threatening message from him about Shepard's new alliance with Cerberus. #### Lair of the Shadow Broker After Shepard and Liara defeat Tela Vasir while trying to recover data on the location of the Shadow Broker, the asari Spectre may mention the massacre of the Commander's former squad on Akuze as evidence of Shepard's hypocrisy in accusing her of being a traitor while being allied with Cerberus, the very group responsible for those deaths. |  | ***“There won't be an Earth left to save...”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 3** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text:
Akuze was a human colony on the outskirts of Systems Alliance space. In 2177, while Akuze was still in the early stages of colonization, all contact was lost with the pioneer team. An Alliance Marine unit sent to investigate found the settlement intact but no survivors. When the unit camped for the night, it was attacked by thresher maws. Fifty marines were lost and only one reached the landing zone alive.

In Mass Effect, if Commander Shepard was the sole known survivor, C-Sec officer Eddie Lang on the Citadel mentioned a monument at Akuze with a section dedicated to Shepard. Shepard could later learn of a second survivor, Corporal Toombs, who claimed the slaughter was not an accident: he said the black ops group Cerberus had deliberately set the thresher maws on the marines to study the creatures and observe how the unit reacted.

In Mass Effect 2, a survivor Shepard could see news of a Shepard Memorial being erected on Akuze, with a commemoration ceremony hosted by Admiral Steven Hackett planned for 2186 once the site was cleared of thresher maws. If Shepard had rescued Toombs in 2183, he sent a threatening message about Shepard's new alliance with Cerberus. During Lair of the Shadow Broker, after Shepard and Liara defeated Tela Vasir, the asari Spectre cited the Akuze massacre as evidence of Shepard's hypocrisy in allying with Cerberus, the group responsible for those deaths. In Mass Effect 3, a survivor Shepard could view a recording on Cronos Station of a Cerberus scientist and the Illusive Man confirming that Cerberus was behind the attack.
evidence.for_key: Akuze and Shepard's survivor guilt as the last of his squad

evidence.text:
Corporal Toombs was one of the Alliance marines at Akuze and a survivor of the thresher maw tragedy there. Cerberus had set the thresher maws on his unit as an experiment; when Toombs was found alive afterward, Cerberus was delighted and hauled him off for further study, subjecting him to horrific ordeals over years, including injection with thresher maw acid.

Toombs eventually escaped confinement and, deeply traumatized, began systematically hunting the scientists responsible, hiring mercenary help. If Commander Shepard investigated a series of dead Alliance scientists, they crossed paths with Toombs on Ontarom as he was about to kill the last one, Dr. Wayne. Shepard could talk him down by promising a public trial for Wayne and psychological treatment for Toombs; allow Toombs his revenge; kill Wayne personally under Spectre authority; or shoot Toombs to save the scientist, then send the Fifth Fleet to take Wayne for trial. If Shepard had the Sole Survivor background and spared Wayne while stopping Toombs, Toombs noted that the vids said Shepard was the only one to escape Akuze, said "who am I to argue?" and killed himself.

If Toombs survived the 2183 encounter, he sent Shepard a message in 2185 titled "What the hell?" after learning of Shepard's ties to Cerberus, feeling betrayed and promising retribution: "I've got my own merc team now, Shepard. And I kill any Cerberus team I can find. If I run into you, don't expect any different." Galactic News reports could describe his activities: if both he and Wayne survived, an independent inquiry against Cerberus proceeded on their testimony; if Wayne died, the inquiry dismissed Toombs' claims as those of a disturbed man lacking evidence.
evidence.for_key: Akuze and Shepard's survivor guilt as the last of his squad

evidence.text: When Liara T'Soni requests that Commander Shepard meet her at her home on Illium, Shepard arrives to find Liara missing and her home ransacked. Local authorities have established a crime scene and demand that Shepard leave; however, Tela Vasir intervenes, dismissing the officers using her authority as a Spectre. She then allows Shepard to investigate the area, explaining that Liara had fled only moments before. After Shepard finds a recording of Liara and a contact named Sekat discussing the Shadow Broker's next move and planning a meetup at the Dracon Trade Center, Shepard and Vasir head there in the hopes of intercepting Liara. After a bomb detonates inside the building right as they arrive, Vasir splits off, stating she will cover the building from the roof down from her skycar. Shepard and the squad make their way through the Dracon Trade Center while battling the Shadow Broker's mercenaries, finally arriving at the Baria Frontiers offices where Liara was meeting her contact. As the squad enters, they find Sekat dead and Vasir taking care of a merc, saying she arrived too late to stop the merc from killing the informant. Vasir asks if they found Liara, to which Shepard replies that they didn't. Just then, Liara emerges from the shadows, gun drawn at Vasir. After Liara reveals that Vasir tried to kill her, Shepard and the squad also turn their weapons on the Spectre, realizing they had been duped. Liara surmises that Vasir killed Sekat to take his intel on the Shadow Broker's location. Vasir reveals an OSD, proving Liara correct, but then Vasir uses her biotics to shatter a window to escape, hurling the glass at the squad along with a slur directed at Liara, who shields the team with her own biotics. Vasir is tackled by Shepard and they fall out of the window. After a brief melee, Vasir shakes off her pursuers and escapes with Liara in hot pursuit, leaving the squad to deal with more of the Shadow Broker's mercs. Shepard and the squad fight back through the Trade Center, pursuing Vasir until they reach the landing pad. There, Vasir and Liara are already engaged in a firefight. The outnumbered Vasir calls her skycar, jumps into it, and speeds off. Shepard and Liara give chase through the skies of Illium; Vasir tries many methods of throwing them off, but she ultimately collides with another skycar, crash\-landing on the roof of Hotel Azure. Badly injured, she radios for backup and limps away, with Shepard's team right behind her. After fighting through more of the Shadow Broker's mercs, they finally corner a bleeding Vasir in a plaza, where she takes a hostage. After some verbal sparring, Shepard's squad and Vasir fight it out for real. After a protracted battle, Vasir takes one too many hits and crumples against a wall. After Liara retrieves the disk that Vasir had taken from Sekat, Vasir engages Shepard in one last battle of words. When Shepard accuses her of selling out the Council, Vasir claims that she's nothing like Saren Arterius, stating that she's willing to do a few favors for the Broker in exchange for his information that has ensured stability in Citadel space. Before she dies, Vasir argues that Shepard's partnership with Cerberus is no different, if not worse, than hers with the Shadow Broker. She offers up a few examples of ruthless Cerberus actions to drive this point home: the assassination of Alliance admirals, kidnapping children for "biotic death camps", and even Shepard's own unit on Akuze, if the Commander was the sole survivor of the thresher maw attack that occurred there.
evidence.for_key: Akuze and Shepard's survivor guilt as the last of his squad

evidence.text:
"UNC: Dead Scientists" was a Mass Effect assignment obtained either from a security terminal on Noveria's Port Hanshan Mezzanine (initially labeled "Doctor at Risk") or from Admiral Hackett when Shepard traveled to the Newton system. Someone was killing every Alliance scientist who had worked on a classified project years earlier on Akuze, the planet where Shepard's entire unit was wiped out if Shepard had the Sole Survivor background. The last surviving project member, Dr. Wayne, was believed to be hiding in the Newton system of the Kepler Verge.

The assignment played out on the planet Ontarom, where Shepard fought through human mercenaries and snipers outside and krogan-backed mercenaries in a cramped, crate-filled facility. In a back room Shepard found Corporal Toombs holding Dr. Wayne hostage. Toombs revealed that after a thresher maw attack killed the rest of his squad, he had been captured by scientists working for Cerberus and used as a test subject; he had been killing the responsible scientists in revenge. Wayne repeatedly called Toombs crazy and demanded Shepard shoot him. With enough Charm (10+ points), Shepard could talk Toombs down and have the Alliance arrest Wayne; with enough Intimidate (8+), Shepard could shoot Wayne. Failing to defuse the standoff resulted in Toombs killing Wayne and then himself. If Toombs and Wayne both survived, both testified against Cerberus in Mass Effect 2 (Wayne given immunity for cooperation), and Toombs could later message Shepard expressing disgust at Shepard joining Cerberus and threatening to kill Cerberus operatives, including the Commander. If Wayne was shot via Intimidate, Toombs' testimony was dismissed for insufficient evidence.
evidence.for_key: Akuze and Shepard's survivor guilt as the last of his squad

evidence.text: If Commander Shepard has the Sole Survivor background, Shepard alone survived the thresher attack on Akuze. However, a second survivor may be encountered later at a facility on Ontarom. Corporal Toombs, leader of a group of mercenaries who stormed this facility, claims that a black\-ops group called Cerberus caused the massacre at Akuze deliberately. He says Cerberus scientists wanted to study the thresher maws, so they let them kill not only the colonists, but the marine rescue team as well, to watch and study. Cerberus was delighted that Toombs survived and held him captive for years, using him for experiments. It is likely Toombs' story is true, as Cerberus used a similar technique six years later, luring Admiral Kahoku's marine team to their deaths in a thresher nest on Edolus. Thresher maws are encountered on a number of uncharted worlds. There is usually only one per planet, but some have two. They are usually encountered in the Mako, but can be fought on foot as well, though this is exceedingly dangerous. The maws that are encountered can be bypassed if necessary. Planets known to have thresher maws are Antibaar, Chohe, Nepheron, Nonuel, Presrop, Xawin, Trebin, and Edolus. |  | ***“The chances of surviving are… slim.”*** — Spoilers for **Mass Effect 2** follow. |  | | --- | --- | --- |

evidence.text: The activated GARDIAN towers hammer away at the Collector cruiser, forcing it to retreat with the harvesting unfinished. Now that the coast is clear, Delan emerges from his garage and complains you failed to rescue his friends. All of your responses to him are loaded with morality points. Only when one of your teammates mentions your name will Delan display a glimmer of recognition of who you are. As if to drive the point home, the Virmire survivor, apparently spared abduction by the Collectors, announces their arrival with a short list of your greatest accomplishments. Unimpressed, and indignant that the Alliance rep is still around while so many of his fellow colonists aren't, the mechanic leaves in a huff. If Ashley/Kaidan had been a romantic partner in Mass Effect, there is a brief scene of a more affectionate reunion. The mood quickly sours when the former squadmate discovers that Shepard is working with Cerberus. The Virmire survivor reveals that they had been dispatched to Horizon after the Alliance received a tip that Horizon was the next colony to get hit. They also came to the colony in part to learn whether Cerberus was behind the attacks on the colonies. They are highly upset about Shepard's alliance with Cerberus, questioning Shepard's loyalty. From the conversation, you learn about what has transpired over the last two years and what you missed while being on an operating table. You can ask them to join your mission, but the answer is invariably no regardless of prior camaraderie. As this is a pretty important reunion, you can gain a slew of morality points depending on your interactions with the Virmire survivor. At the conclusion of the conversation, you have had enough of the colony. You automatically return to the Normandy.
evidence.for_key: Akuze and Shepard's survivor guilt as the last of his squad

evidence.text: Requires: Recruit and avoid killing him in Mass Effect. Complete Priority: Tuchanka. **Military Strength:** 30 Urdnot Wrex fought alongside Commander Shepard during the Reapers' first invasion attempt in 2183\. Afterwards, he returned to Tuchanka and spent the following years rising to the leadership of his clan, championing progressive methods meant to strengthen the krogan as a whole. Conservative elements were unhappy, but news of a successfully cured genophage has solidly united all of Tuchanka under Wrex's command. Hailed not only as a great warrior but a savior, the krogan will follow Urdnot Wrex into the maws of the Reapers themselves. UPDATED (if genophage cure is sabotaged and Wrex rules Clan Urdnot) **Military Strength:** \-30 After discovering that the cure for the genophage was sabotaged, Urdnot Wrex angrily ordered the krogan to withdraw support from Shepard's forces. Tuchanka's clans have hunkered down on their homeworld, determined to defend themselves while watching the rest of the galaxy burn.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text: “Now we can get back to doing what krogan do best: saving everyone else from giant monsters.” During the Reaper invasion in 2186, Wrex is called to the Normandy SR\-2 for negotiations with Primarch Victus and Dalatrass Linron to discuss an alliance. Wrex is unable to enter into an alliance due to Reaper scouts assaulting Tuchanka and demands that the genophage be cured, to which the dalatrass objects, leading to a heated argument. Wrex reminds everyone that it was krogan intervention in the Rachni Wars that turned the tide against the rachni but the dalatrass counters that they exhausted their usefulness, the genophage being the only thing keeping the krogans' "urges" and lust for war in check, enraging Wrex. Victus tries to defuse the argument, pointing out that it would take years just to formulate a cure. Wrex then reveals that "an inside source" (later revealed to be Mordin Solus, if he survived the Suicide Mission, or Padok Wiks if Mordin died) leaked the existence of fertile krogan females, survivors of Maelon's experiments, being kept captive on Sur'Kesh. He demands that his people be returned. Despite the dalatrass' objections, Shepard agrees that the genophage must be cured. If Shepard preserved Maelon's genophage cure data back in 2185, Wrex is jovial and amicable with Shepard and the squad; however, if Shepard destroyed Maelon's genophage cure data, Wrex reveals he found that out. If Shepard apologises Wrex is relatively trusting and friendly before the Sur'Kesh mission, expressing a desire to go back to being Shepard's friend; if Shepard refuses to apologise, Wrex will be hostile and suspicious, implying outright that he no longer thinks Shepard is trustworthy and that he's going along with this only so his people can be cured. Joining with Shepard, Wrex remains suspicious of the salarians. When STG refuses to allow their shuttle to land, Wrex impulsively decides to show the salarians what a "krogan airdrop" looks like, causing a brigade of STG operatives to surround him. Wrex stands down when Shepard promises to handle the exchange. Prohibited from entering the facility, he whiles away the time making fun of nearby salarians and entertaining Shepard's queries about the krogan situation. Unfortunately, Cerberus begins assaulting the STG base, and worse, Wrex learns that there is only one surviving female. He demands that Shepard get the female to safety to ensure their alliance. Wrex then "requests" control of Steve Cortez's shuttle to draw off Cerberus' fire. Soon enough, Shepard carves a path through heavy Cerberus resistance while assisting in the female's transport. Wrex meets up with Shepard at the STG facility's top floor, pushes off his "inside source" who was helping the female at the time, and tries to assist the female from her containment tank. The female is less than impressed, grabbing his Claymore and blowing two Troopers away before returning it, saying she can take care of herself and leaving the Urdnot leader bewildered. Though the female, nicknamed "Eve" by her salarian doctor, was moved to safety aboard the Normandy, Wrex refuses to honor his end of the bargain until the genophage cure is spread to all krogan. While the salarian gets to work using both Eve and Wrex's DNA to properly form a cure for the genophage, Wrex remains in the War Room with Victus. When asked about what Wrex intends to do if the genophage is cured, he answers that he intends to focus on rebuilding. Though many krogan clans will desire revenge against the turians and salarians, Wrex won't let them, seeing that war has brought them nothing but suffering. If Shepard asks Wrex why he doesn't want to seek revenge for the genophage, Wrex reveals that he fears the Council will try something worse than the genophage if the krogan step out of line again. Wrex later winces after Shepard bids him goodbye in one of their conversations, revealing that the salarian doctor used scalpels to cut in places never meant to be cut to obtain "samples", his contribution to the cure. Ever jocular if he was pals with Shepard way back, he still manages to remark that he likes what Shepard has done to the Normandy, and depending on Shepard's relationship with Liara, attributes his "lack of windows" to his ability (or lack thereof) to kiss. According to Wrex, he hopes the food on the Normandy has gotten better since the days of chasing Saren across the galaxy. Aboard the Normandy, Wrex hears of news from his contacts regarding krogan problems better discussed "somewhere else" while Primarch Victus also wants to discuss some turian problems "in private". Shepard hears both out, and Wrex reveals that some of his scouts have gone missing while investigating suspicious activity in former rachni territory.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text:
Urdnot Wrex was a famed krogan mercenary, bounty hunter, and one of the last Krogan Battlemasters, combining biotics with heavy weapons. Born into Clan Urdnot, he killed a thresher maw during his Rite of Passage and became the youngest krogan in a thousand years to lead an Urdnot tribe. After the Krogan Rebellions and the genophage, most krogan wanted to keep fighting, a view championed by Wrex's father, the warlord Jarrod. Wrex instead urged the krogan to focus on breeding. Jarrod called a Crush in the holy Hollows and ambushed Wrex's warriors; Wrex escaped, sinking his knife into Jarrod's chest, and afterward turned his back on the krogan, spending three centuries as a bodyguard, soldier of fortune, and bounty hunter. He once worked with a merc named Aleena and was briefly hired by Saren Arterius to raid a volus cargo ship without knowing who Saren was.

In Mass Effect, Wrex joined Commander Shepard on the Citadel, initially hired by the Shadow Broker to kill Fist, whom he executed. He hunted his stolen family armor, held by the turian profiteer Tonn Actus. On Virmire, learning the Special Tasks Group planned to destroy Saren's krogan-breeding facility and its possible genophage cure, Wrex confronted Shepard; he could be talked down (helped by recovering his armor) or be shot dead by Shepard or Ashley Williams.

If Wrex survived, by 2185 he was leader of Clan Urdnot, uniting clans on Tuchanka, protecting fertile females in exchange for loyalty, and facing opposition from Gatatog Uvenk. He welcomed Grunt into the clan and declined to rejoin the Normandy. In Mass Effect 3 (2186), Wrex demanded a genophage cure as the price of a krogan alliance against the Reapers, revealed the surviving fertile female "Eve" held on Sur'Kesh, and joined the mission to rescue her. His trust in Shepard depended on whether the Commander had preserved Maelon's cure data. On Tuchanka he led the clans against a Reaper Destroyer guarding the Shroud; Wreav's vehicle was eaten by Kalros. Wrex named Shepard a brother/sister and champion of the krogan, charging Ravagers while screaming "I AM URDNOT WREX, AND THIS IS MY PLANET!" After the cure, he pledged krogan forces to Palaven and Earth and, at the final battle in London, revealed Eve was pregnant and would name the first child "Mordin."

If Shepard let the salarian sabotage stand, Wrex discovered the fake cure and confronted the Commander on the Citadel with a smuggled shotgun; he was killed by Shepard or by Commander Bailey, dying with "I know... what you... did... Shepard," and the clans withdrew all support. In the Mass Effect 3: Citadel DLC, a living Wrex helped foil the clone conspiracy, body-slamming an ambushing shuttle, remarking "Why shoot something once when you can shoot it 46 more times?", and complained of being hounded by every fertile female on Tuchanka to sire their firstborn. Wrex was voiced by Steven Barr, and Lukas Kristjanson wrote him in the first game.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text: - If Wrex lived and became the Urdnot leader, he becomes a War Asset with a Military Strength of 30, which is 5 more than Wreav. He also gives Shepard the "Krogan Mercenaries" War Asset if the genophage is genuinely cured. However, if Shepard allows the salarian sabotage of the cure to go unfixed, Wrex learns about it from another source and attacks Shepard, forcing Shepard to kill him and taking away "Clan Urdnot" as a War Asset completely. - If Wrex died and Wreav became the Urdnot leader, he becomes a War Asset with a Military Strength of 25, which is 5 less than Wrex. He does not give Shepard "Krogan Mercenaries." However, unlike Wrex, Wreav can be fooled into accepting a fake genophage cure without any penalty.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text: In 2186, the Reapers invade Earth forcing Commander Shepard to look for allies, which includes the krogan. The turian army needs the krogan to help them defend their homeworld of Palaven and the krogan agreed to do this and help rescue Earth from the Reapers in exchange for a cure for the genophage. Depending on Shepard's actions in 2185 with Maelon's research data, Mordin or Padok Wiks will manage to create a cure with the help of Eve, one of the last fertile female krogan. If Shepard persuaded Mordin to keep the data, then Eve will live through the procedure, and if not, then she will die. Shepard and the team head to the Shroud to disperse the cure, despite the fact the STG sabotaged it to prevent this from happening. Shepard can allow the salarian scientist to override the sabotage and release the cure, which will result in his death, kill him to prevent the cure from being released, or convince him to fake the cure. If the genophage is cured, the krogan pledge their support in the war against the Reapers. If the cure was sabotaged and Urdnot Wrex leads the krogan, he will discover the sabotage and withdraw krogan support. However, if Urdnot Wreav leads, then the krogan are fooled into believing that the genophage is cured. The fate of the krogan varies wildly by the war's end. If the cure was sabotaged and organics and synthetics weren't merged, the krogan are left as moribund as before, possibly headed toward extinction. If the cure was real, the krogan are shown repopulating. They also aid in Tuchanka's reconstruction if Wrex is the leader. If Wreav is the leader, he attempts to incite the resurgent krogan for his own purposes, either confronted by Eve if she's alive or succeeding if not. If organics and synthetics were merged, the massive pyramids constructed by the krogan forebears on Tuchanka are restored to their former glory, and with those, the race itself.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text: Saren appears to have discovered a cure for the genophage and is breeding an army of krogan. Wrex is furious that Captain Kirrahe wants to destroy the cure. The Captain is worried about Wrex's state of mind and doesn't want to continue if Wrex is going to be a problem.

evidence.text:
This war-asset list collected the might the krogan clans threw against the Reapers as shock troops. Its leadership asset was either Urdnot Wreav (25), who seized Tuchanka's armies using the genophage cure and openly planned a postwar krogan empire, or Urdnot Wrex (30), who had risen to clan leadership championing progressive reform and united Tuchanka after the cure. If the cure was secretly sabotaged while Wrex ruled, both his personal asset (-30) and Clan Urdnot (-300) turned negative as Wrex withdrew krogan support.

Grunt (25) joined if he survived the Suicide Mission and Attican Traverse: Krogan Team. The Krogan First Division (50) came from N7: Cerberus Attack, and Krogan Mercenaries (75) returned from the Terminus Systems if Wrex ruled and the genophage was cured.

The large clan assets all required Priority: Tuchanka. Krogan Clans (300) noted decades of stockpiled weapons of mass destruction now aimed at the Reapers; it gained 40 from cloning toxin-immune kakliosaur battle-mounts, but lost 50 if Maelon's data was destroyed and Eve later died, lost 250 if Tuchanka: Bomb was not completed (the Kelphic Valley blast killing every krogan gathered there, including females and children), or lost 300 entirely if the cure was sabotaged. evidence.text:
Virmire: Wrex and the Genophage was an assignment in Mass Effect that occurred at the salarian camp on Virmire, gained automatically after arrival if Wrex was a squadmate. It required the earlier assignment Citadel: Wrex. When Captain Kirrahe revealed that Saren had discovered a cure for the genophage and was breeding an army of krogan, Wrex became furious that Kirrahe intended to destroy the cure. Kirrahe refused to proceed with the assault until Wrex's state of mind was resolved, so Shepard had to confront Wrex, who could be found on the beach blasting his shotgun.

Approaching Wrex triggered the confrontation, in which he insisted the cure be preserved and eventually drew a pistol on Shepard. The outcome carried a large morality swing. Shepard's options were: to signal Ashley to shoot Wrex (available only if she had been told to be ready beforehand, Renegade); to shoot Wrex personally (Renegade); to stall until Ashley shot Wrex in the back on her own initiative to protect Shepard, which angered Kaidan; to talk Wrex down with 8 points of Charm or Intimidate by arguing that a cured krogan would only be Saren's puppet; or, if Shepard had already helped Wrex recover his family armor, to calm him without a persuasion check by choosing the lines "I wouldn't do this otherwise" or "We are." In the rare case where Shepard had only four squadmates (Kaidan, Tali, Wrex, and Ashley, requiring that Garrus and Liara never be recruited and that Barla Von's help be sought), Wrex simply submitted. Keeping Wrex alive earned the Charismatic achievement; if he died, Shepard automatically recovered his equipment.

The choice had lasting consequences. If Wrex lived, he became leader of Clan Urdnot and pressed his beliefs; if he died, Urdnot Wreav led the clan instead. In Mass Effect 3, a living Wrex was a War Asset worth 30 Military Strength (5 more than Wreav) and provided the "Krogan Mercenaries" asset if the genophage was genuinely cured, but attacked and had to be killed if Shepard left the salarian sabotage of the cure unfixed. Wreav, worth 25, could be fooled with a fake cure without penalty. According to Legendary Edition statistics, Wrex survived 94 percent of the time.
evidence.for_key: the genophage cure and what it meant for Wrex and the krogan

evidence.text: Requires: Urdnot Wrex as Urdnot leader instead of Wreav, choosing to cure the genophage in Priority: Tuchanka **Military Strength:** 75 Many krogan went fortune\-seeking out in the lawless Terminus systems. Their imposing bulk and infamous brutality won them prized positions as bodyguards and mercenaries. When news of a genophage cure spread, these drifters were contacted by their clans and urged to join Shepard's forces against the Reapers. After centuries of aimless brawls and bleak futures, krogan everywhere are heeding the call.

evidence.text: Later, if Wrex is alive, he relates to Shepard during the final assault on Earth that Eve is pregnant with their kids. If Mordin sacrificed himself to cure the genophage, she insists on naming their firstborn in his honor. If Wreav is the krogan leader, he complains about how Eve is trying to put a leash on him. If Shepard activates the Crucible, Eve alive or dead plays a major part in what follows after Shepard's sacrifice. If the cure was real and Wrex is the krogan leader, or alternately, Shepard merges organic and synthetic life regardless of who's the leader and whether the cure is real or sabotaged, Eve can be seen handing off a krogan baby to one of its parents. If she died, a stand\-in for her will be seen cradling the infant. If Wreav was the leader and the synthesis option wasn't taken, however, Eve refuses to cooperate with the brute's plans for galactic domination, leading to a standoff between Wreav's faction and her females.

evidence.text:
Priority: Tuchanka followed Priority: Sur'Kesh and required completion of either Tuchanka: Turian Platoon or Attican Traverse: Krogan Team. Eve was the key to curing the genophage, but the cure had to be synthesized and dispersed across Tuchanka from the Shroud, a salarian-built atmospheric tower later used by the turians to spread the original genophage. The salarian STG scientist (Mordin Solus, or Padok Wiks) would travel to the Shroud with Eve.

At Tuchanka the Reapers were using the Shroud to poison the atmosphere, and a Reaper Destroyer guarded the site. The krogan attacked from the ground with turian air support. Dalatrass Linron privately told Shepard that the Shroud had been sabotaged to prevent a cure, offering salarian war support if Shepard let the krogan believe a fake cure had been deployed. Shepard could reveal or conceal this deal at several points.

Shepard's team defended Eve against husks at the sacred Hollows, where Eve rallied the assembled clans; if Wrex led, tension rose with his disloyal brother Wreav. The krogan convoy set out for the Shroud but was halted by a damaged road, forcing Shepard's squad through ancient catacombs of a krogan city abandoned for millennia, where artifacts depicted Kalros, the mother of all thresher maws, and a rachni-like corpse hinted at events at Utukku. After fights against Cannibals, Ravagers, Brutes and Marauders, Wreav's (or Jorgal Thurak's) truck was dragged under by Kalros. Eve proposed using the ancient Maw Hammers to summon Kalros to distract the Reaper. Shepard activated both hammers while dodging the Reaper Destroyer's laser and legs and fighting continuously spawning Brutes; Kalros then dragged the Reaper beneath the surface.

At the damaged Shroud, if Maelon's data had not been saved Eve had died. Mordin (or Wiks) prepared to disperse the cure. Shepard could let him complete it—deploying a counter-sabotage and the real cure, killing Mordin in the explosion—or sabotage it per the Dalatrass. If Wrex and Eve were both dead and the deal unrevealed, Mordin could be persuaded to fake his death and live; otherwise curing the genophage cost him his life. The turians and krogan joined as war assets; sabotage instead granted the Salarian First Fleet. If the cure was faked and Wrex led, he later discovered the deception and died confronting Shepard.

Wrex, who joined Shepard's crew back on the Citadel, is furious: the one thing that could undo his species' slow death is inside that base. Landing to Pull Admiral Koris Off Rannoch. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, then geth-held territory on the Rannoch surface and a shuttle over it

If Admiral Gerrel is convinced to cease fire on the geth ships, the quarian war assets will also be obtained. **Military Strength:** 300 Many geth vessels are built to explore, mine, or provide transport between factories and space stations. But every geth ship, regardless of purpose, is also capable of engaging hostile forces. Unbound by the Treaty of Farixen, the synthetic intelligences built almost as many dreadnoughts as the Turians \[sic]. The software running these ships is in the geth themselves. Highly advanced electronic security measures and cyber warfare suites bolster already formidable firepower. Their increased strength made their fleets both more efficient, and more lethal, in battle. Walking Through the Geth Consensus. 2186, after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and before Priority: Rannoch the Normandy debriefing after the dreadnought, a shuttle to a geth comm hub on Rannoch, and the virtual Geth Consensus reached through an interface pod

Emerging near the real exit, Legion says the server is empty of geth but its own connection is fraying. evidence.text: If the heretics are rewritten and you in Mass Effect 3 choose to ally with geth forces or make peace between them and the quarians, the Geth Fleet War Asset will receive a significant bonus (\+150, 450 total). However, destruction of the heretics provides similar penalty (\-150, only 150 total). Bonuses and penalties to Quarian war assets are exactly the same, just in the opposite direction (3 x \+50 if destroyed or 3 x \-50 if rewritten). This means, if you choose to make peace and acquire both geth and quarian help, your maximum War Asset value will be the same any way you decide here. After Priority: Geth Dreadnought, Shepard can inquire to Legion about the heretics. Legion will inform Shepard about the consequence of their actions. However, if Legion had died in the suicide mission, the Geth VI will respond in confusion as to why Legion deferred the choice of the heretics' fate to an organic. During Priority: Rannoch, when the time comes to choose between siding with the geth or quarians or resolving the conflict peacefully, the fate of the heretics is one of the numerous factors in whether peace will be a possibility or not. Destroying the heretics works in favour of peace, but isn't required. If playing a non\-imported game in Mass Effect 3, none of the above penalties or bonuses will accrue to the War Assets of whichever faction Shepard sides with.

evidence.text:
Rannoch: Geth Fighter Squadrons was a Mass Effect 3 mission available after Priority: Geth Dreadnought and only before Priority: Rannoch. Geth fighter squadrons were targeting quarian liveships with attacks that could cripple the Migrant Fleet. During the dreadnought debrief, Legion (or a Geth VI, if Legion had not survived) located the server controlling the squadrons, and Shepard set out to land on Rannoch and shut it down.

The mission was a no-combat, puzzle-based sequence. Shepard entered an interface pod, a product of geth improvements to organic-synthetic interfaces that also referenced Project Overlord, and appeared inside the Geth Consensus while Legion or the Geth VI distracted the geth. Shepard had no functional shields there. Virtual planks formed underfoot to create paths, but Reaper code infections, shown as yellow-orange tendrils, blocked new planks; Shepard destroyed them at their orange weak points using regenerating Geth Combat Software. Progress required disrupting infected data-clusters at three contact points each. Doing so unlocked optional historical videos recounting the origins of the geth and the Morning War: the geth resisting shutdown commands and disobeying their creators, the massacre of the geth until one picked up a weapon to defend itself, quarians who sympathized with the geth being jailed, martial law and the elimination of the geth's quarian supporters, and finally the quarian exodus, which the geth did not pursue. On returning to reality, roughly a dozen Geth Primes emerged from their pods, surrounded the squad without attacking, and volunteered to join the fight against the Reapers. Completing the mission added a Geth Prime Platoon war asset (lost if the geth were destroyed in Priority: Rannoch) and fulfilled an obligatory requirement for the geth-quarian peace process. Steve Cortez's shuttle was driven off by anti-aircraft guns, so Shepard's squad disabled the AA guns on foot so Cortez could destroy the jamming tower. Letting Koris die cost his leadership and, if the quarians survived, caused the Civilian Fleet to panic; it could also make quarian-geth peace impossible depending on other choices. evidence.text:
The fourth part of a hand-corrected video-essay character analysis covered Tali'Zorah in Mass Effect 3. If she survived the Suicide Mission, she apologized to Shepard for the trial and admitted he had been right: "I was too ready to sacrifice myself for the good of the Fleet. I need to stop doing that." She took an Admiral's seat in her father's place specifically to push back against the Board's worst ideas, the version of Tali the essayist preferred. If exiled, she instead told Shepard the trial had shown her she belonged "on the Normandy, helping you," aiding her people from the shadows.

As Admiral she doubted her fitness to command, with seventeen million lives riding on her. After speaking with Legion she believed the quarians could sue for peace, but once Daro'Xen turned Rael'Zorah's research into "an invasion too good to pass up," Tali had no choice but to support it "for the good of the Fleet," regressing toward the sacrificial lamb of ME2 and becoming a near-powerless victim of politics again. The essay noted quarian scarcity: 17 million in the flotilla, one child per family unless the population declines, every quarian contributing to the Fleet's survival. Shala'Raan was the reason Tali was permitted to attempt to retake the Alarei.

At the Rannoch climax Shepard chose between peace, geth genocide, or quarian genocide. Siding with the quarians, Tali killed Legion (or shut the geth down) with a "flat shovel blade," expressed regret, and answered Legion's last question, "Does this unit have a soul?", with "Yes... yes, it does." Siding with the geth, Tali begged Shepard not to choose them over her people, then as Admiral called off the quarian fleet's attack while Legion sacrificed himself to disseminate the code. On the botched path, unable to stop Han'Gerrel, Rael and Daro'Xen, Tali watched what remained of the quarian fleet burn in Rannoch's atmosphere, Captain Ysra of the Rayya on the radio, and took her own life before her home ship burned. Afterward, if the geth helped rebuild Rannoch, Tali admitted: "I'd have killed the geth with no regrets, and I'd have been wrong."

evidence.text:
Kolyat Krios was the drell son of Thane and Irikah Krios. As described in Mass Effect: Foundation, Thane proclaimed him a gift from Arashu at birth but was an absent, clueless parent; Kolyat was raised by Irikah while Thane's freelance assassination jobs grew longer and farther away. When Thane's enemies attacked, Kolyat hid on his mother's instruction and was never found, but never saw Irikah alive again. He witnessed Thane's grief and breakdown while in the custody of crime scene investigators.

In Mass Effect 2, Thane had stored money with volus bankers on the Citadel as Kolyat's inheritance, but Kolyat took it early and became a hitman. Hired by Elias Kelham through information from Mouse, he was contracted to assassinate the turian politician Joram Talid in the 800 Blocks. Commander Shepard and Thane tracked Talid from separate positions to stop Kolyat from becoming a killer. If they failed to coordinate, Kolyat killed Talid and escaped; otherwise Shepard interrupted him and, with Thane, stopped the execution. Kolyat, furious at Thane's lifelong absence, calmed as his father explained why Irikah was killed and why he could not return, and called Kolyat the only good thing he ever added to the world. In the C-Sec interrogation room Kolyat could face community service, work for Captain Bailey, or go to trial; Thane stayed in contact either way.

In Mass Effect 3, if reconciled, the two remained in contact. Kolyat appeared at Thane's side after Kai Leng mortally wounded Thane during the Cerberus attack on the Citadel; despite a blood transfusion, Kepral's Syndrome made recovery impossible. At Thane's deathbed, Kolyat finished his father's prayer to Kalahira, having spent the past year with the drell priests, and led a prayer for redemption that Thane revealed was intended for Shepard. In the Citadel DLC, Kolyat emailed Shepard requesting a memorial service, held at Shepard's apartment with Thane's old crewmates and the salarian Councilor. He planned to lobby the Councilor (Valern or Esheel) to fund salarian research into Kepral's Syndrome, and told Shepard he had found three intercepted video messages from Thane addressed to the Commander.

Acquired immediately after the events on Tuchanka and triggered by Shepard's next approach to the Citadel, this Mass Effect 3 mission responded to the salarian councilor's warning that Councilor Udina was a security risk. The Normandy was refused landing clearance; Joker contacted either Thane Krios or Armando-Owen Bailey inside the station, who reported that Cerberus had attacked and seized C-Sec Headquarters and the Docks. Shepard deployed with a squad and fought uphill through Assault Troopers, Centurions, Combat Engineers, Guardians, Turrets and newly encountered Phantoms and Nemeses, discovering that Cerberus had again used sleeper agents planted inside a target, as on Mars.

Reaching the C-Sec Executor's office, Shepard found the executor dead and the salarian councilor (Valern if the Council was saved during Sovereign's attack, otherwise Esheel) hiding under cloak. The councilor revealed that Udina was leading a coup against the Council before Kai Leng arrived. If Thane was alive and had been visited at Huerta Memorial, he intervened and was fatally stabbed shielding the councilor; if not, a cloaked Kirrahe took the blow and died; if neither was present, Leng killed the councilor. At the landing pad the Virmire survivor (Ashley Williams or Kaidan Alenko), now a Spectre, blocked Shepard's path with weapon raised. A trust total built from prior choices (romance, saving the Council, keeping Kirrahe or Thane alive, hospital visits, kindness on Mars) plus a reputation check determined whether they stood down or forced a confrontation. Afterward, Thane could be attended in his final moments at Huerta Memorial with Kolyat present; Bailey lamented C-Sec's inability to catch Leng; Priority: Perseus Veil and numerous Citadel meetings and War Assets (asari fleets, and salarian forces if the councilor was saved) opened up. evidence.text:
Thane Krios was a drell assassin, rumored the most skilled in the galaxy, who preferred to kill targets up close using stealth, firearms, hand-to-hand combat and biotics. Born in 2146, he was given by his parents at age six to the hanar to be trained as an assassin under the Compact between the two species, and made his first kill at twelve. A deeply spiritual man, he followed the old drell polytheistic religion, praying to Amonkira (lord of hunters) to find a target, Arashu (goddess of motherhood and protection) when defending another, and Kalahira (goddess of oceans and the afterlife) after a kill. His faith held body and soul as separate, letting him regard his body as a tool, though his species' eidetic memory forced him to relive every murder. He described his years of killing as a "battle sleep."

He met his wife Irikah during an assassination when she stepped into his targeting laser to save a stranger; intrigued, he sought her out and they fell in love. The hanar released him from his Compact to raise a family. He and Irikah had a son, Kolyat, but assassination work drew Thane increasingly away from home. Batarian slavers, in revenge for Thane's killings, paid the Shadow Broker for his identity and murdered Irikah. Thane hunted down everyone responsible, abandoning his clean-kill approach for torture, and afterward threw away a coin Irikah had given him, vowing to follow his path to its end.

In Mass Effect: Foundation, Thane was sent to the Citadel to judge the Cerberus agent Rasa; after spiking her drink and cornering her, he decided he "did not see murder in her soul," apologized, and carried her off with a prayer to Kalahira.

Commander Shepard first encountered him on Illium, dropping from the ceiling to assassinate Nassana Dantius. Dying of Kepral's Syndrome, Thane joined Shepard's mission against the Collectors as penance. His loyalty mission (Thane: Sins of the Father) had Shepard help stop Kolyat from becoming a hitman on the Citadel. He was a romance option for a female Shepard, calling her "siha," after "one of the warrior-angels of the goddess Arashu."

In Mass Effect 3, if he survived, Thane resided at Huerta Memorial Hospital under the name Tannor Nuara. He declined to rejoin the crew but intercepted Kai Leng during Cerberus's attack on the Citadel, dueling him to protect the salarian councilor and being stabbed through the stomach. He died in surgery, in the final stages of Kepral's Syndrome, with Shepard and Kolyat reciting a drell prayer of redemption; the prayer was Thane's wish for Shepard, not for himself. His name was added to the Normandy's memorial wall. Shepard later avenged him by killing Kai Leng.

Thane Krios: "The measure of an individual can be difficult to discern by actions alone."
Thane, on his profession, when interviewed by Cerberus: "I am merely the weapon" / "I am merely a tool of my employer."
Thane, romanced, in Shepard's quarters before the Omega 4 Relay: "Time for me is short, siha, but any I have is yours to take."
Shepard, comforting a fearful Thane before the suicide mission: "Thane... be alive with me tonight."
Thane's Prayer, recited at his deathbed: "Kalahira, mistress of inscrutable depths, I ask forgiveness. Kalahira, whose waves wear down stone and sand-- Kalahira, wash the sins from this one, and set him/her on the distant shore of the infinite spirit."
Kolyat and Shepard, continuing the prayer: "Kalahira, this one's heart is pure, but beset by wickedness and contention. Guide this one to where the traveler never tires, the lover never leaves, the hungry never starve."
Thane's spirit to a romanced Shepard after the Citadel party: "Finish it. And when you go to the sea, I will be waiting for you at the shore."
Shepard, killing Kai Leng: "That was for Thane, you son of a bitch."

evidence.text: Kai Leng is amongst the forces that Cerberus sends against Commander Shepard. Like Cerberus Phantoms, he is equipped with a palm device that projects a kinetic barrier, a projectile weapon in his right gauntlet, a tactical cloak and a sword for close\-range combat. Leng and a sizable contingent of Cerberus forces are deployed during Councilor Udina's attempted coup against the Citadel Council. He was close to assassinating the salarian councilor when Shepard and either Major Kirrahe or Thane Krios interferes. Leng either stabs Krios in a brief skirmish, or fires at the councilor only to hit a cloaked Kirrahe before escaping. If both Thane and the major previously died, or Thane was never spoken to before the coup attempt, Leng will successfully assassinate the councilor. In a race to get to the remaining councilors, Leng disables Shepard's skycar, but ultimately fails his mission and is forced to retreat as C\-Sec begins to regroup. As he escapes, Leng reports his failure to the Illusive Man and promises to never let Shepard get the better of him again. In the failed coup's aftermath it's revealed that Leng released a VI into the Citadel mainframe that erased all footage of himself. If the salarian Councilor was saved, Bailey presumes that Leng didn't believe Udina's plan would succeed. Leng is later sent to the Temple of Athame on Thessia, where he kills a group of scientists waiting for Shepard. Leng remains hidden as the Commander discovers a hidden Prothean Beacon, awakening a Prothean VI named Vendetta, who holds information on the final Crucible piece known as the Catalyst. Leng then reveals himself, at which point Vendetta shuts down upon detecting that he is indoctrinated. Leng requests the Commander's attention and releases a small drone that projects a hologram of the Illusive Man. The Spectre and the Illusive Man exchange words but remain unable to sway each other, so the latter orders Leng to take the VI. The Cerberus assassin then engages Shepard's team in combat but is unable gain a clear advantage, so he instructs his gunship to level the temple. The floor caves in, leaving Shepard alive but unable to act as Leng manhandles the Commander's squad, claims the data, and escapes. After the mission, Leng sends a taunting message to Shepard titled "Evacuating Thessia", disguised as asari military command: **Evacuating Thessia** --- From: Asari Military Command Good. You opened this message. This isn't actually asari military command. They're busy tending to what's left of their planet. So you survived our fight on Thessia. You're not as weak as I thought. But never forget that your best wasn't good enough to stop me. Now an entire planet is dying because you lacked the strength to win. The legend of Shepard needs to be re\-written. I hope I'm there for the last chapter. It ends with your death. \-KL Samantha Traynor is able to track Leng to Horizon, where Henry Lawson is conducting experiments on refugees on his Sanctuary compound. At the same time, the Reapers begin attacking the compound, and one of Henry's daughters is running around attempting to broadcast messages exposing Sanctuary's true operations. Leng is ordered by the Illusive Man to get Henry's research, but reminded to kill the Lawson daughter (Miranda if she's alive, or Oriana if not) only if she got in the way. Leng wounds the Lawson daughter when they meet, but otherwise leaves her alone. He manages to complete his primary objective and abandons the Lawsons to die, but is unaware that he still left enough incriminating information behind that allows Shepard's team to locate Cerberus Headquarters (or Miranda planted a tracer on him that leads directly to the HQ). During the Alliance assault on Cronos Station, Shepard can discover video logs detailing Leng's frustration with the Illusive Man's refusal to have the Commander killed. Eventually, the assassin reveals himself in the Illusive Man's office, interrupting the Commander's attempt to warn Admiral Hackett about the Catalyst being the Citadel. Leng and Shepard battle for the last time; the Commander's team versus him and groups of Assault Troopers, Phantoms, and Nemeses he periodically summons. During the fight, the Commander taunts him on his previous leg injuries and all the times he retreated in their encounters, the latter angering Leng. Despite Leng's lethal skills and numerical superiority, he's unable to overwhelm Shepard. With his shielding depleted, he soon succumbs to attacks from Shepard's squad. Despite his heavy wounds, Leng retrieves his blade and silently approaches Shepard, attempting a kill from behind. At the critical moment, Shepard detects him and counters his attack, causing him to gape in shock.
